# Tina4 Ruby

> Tina4 Ruby (the `tina4ruby` gem) is a web framework for Ruby 3.1+ with zero runtime gem dependencies: it serves HTTP itself, and routing, ORM, Frond (Twig-compatible) templates, JWT auth, sessions, queues, WebSocket, GraphQL, WSDL/SOAP and Swagger are all built in. Database drivers such as `sqlite3`, `pg` and `mysql2` are application dependencies. It is one of four Tina4 backends (Python, PHP, Ruby, Node.js) that share the same project layout, CLI, template syntax and `.env` variables.

Quick start. Install the Rust `tina4` CLI (`curl -fsSL https://tina4.com/install.sh | sh`, `brew install tina4stack/tap/tina4`, or `irm https://tina4.com/install.ps1 | iex` on Windows), then:

```bash
tina4 init ruby my-app   # the path is required; runs bundle install for you
cd my-app
tina4 serve              # http://localhost:7147 (TINA4_PORT overrides)
```

Add a route by dropping a file in `src/routes/` (auto-discovered):

```ruby
Tina4::Router.get("/api/hello/{name}") do |request, response|
  response.json({ message: "Hello, #{request.params[:name]}!" })
end
```

Gotchas an agent most needs:

- GET routes are public; POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE require a bearer token (or form token) by default. Chain `.no_auth` to open a write route and `.secure` to protect a GET.
- Path placeholders use `{id}` (not `:id`); a typed placeholder such as `{id:int}` converts the value. `request.params` accepts string or symbol keys.
- `response.json(data, status)` and `response.render("page.twig", data)` are the usual returns.
- The entry point is `app.rb`: `require "tina4ruby"` then `Tina4.run!(__dir__)`. The gem was renamed from `tina4` to `tina4ruby`; the namespace is still `Tina4::`.
- ORM models subclass `Tina4::ORM` and declare columns with `integer_field`, `string_field`, ... The table name defaults to the lowercase class name; call `table_name "users"` or set `TINA4_ORM_PLURAL_TABLE_NAMES=true`. Serialise with `to_h` or `to_json`.
- The database comes from `TINA4_DATABASE_URL` (`sqlite:///`, `postgres://`, `mysql://`, `mssql://`, `firebird://`). Change schema only through SQL files in `migrations/`, never in route code.
- The gem's own CLI is `tina4ruby`; the `tina4` CLI forwards `tina4 generate <model|route|crud|migration|...>` to it. Generated write routes are secure by default.

## Docs

- [Quick reference](https://tina4.com/ruby/index.md): one-page cheat sheet of every feature
- [Getting started](https://tina4.com/ruby/01-getting-started.md): install, scaffold, project layout, first route
- [Routing](https://tina4.com/ruby/02-routing.md): methods, path parameters, route groups, auth modifiers, wildcards
- [Request and response](https://tina4.com/ruby/03-request-response.md): request fields, response helpers, status codes, validation, uploads
- [Templates](https://tina4.com/ruby/04-templates.md): Frond template engine, filters, inheritance
- [Database](https://tina4.com/ruby/05-database.md): configuration, parameterised queries, transactions, migrations, seeding
- [ORM](https://tina4.com/ruby/06-orm.md): models, CRUD, relationships, eager loading, soft delete, auto-CRUD
- [Authentication](https://tina4.com/ruby/08-authentication.md): JWT tokens, password hashing, login flow, protecting routes, CSRF
- [Middleware and security](https://tina4.com/ruby/10-middleware-security.md): the middleware pipeline, built-in and custom middleware
- [Queues](https://tina4.com/ruby/12-queues.md): producers, consumers, retries, dead letters, backends
- [Scaffolding](https://tina4.com/ruby/19-scaffolding.md): `tina4 generate` generators
- [CLI](https://tina4.com/ruby/31-cli.md): every `tina4` and `tina4ruby` command
- [Environment variables](https://tina4.com/ruby/33-environment-variables.md): the `.env` reference
- [Deployment](https://tina4.com/ruby/34-deployment.md): production config, Docker, health checks, reverse proxy, scaling
- [Release notes](https://tina4.com/ruby/36-releases.md): what changed in each release
